record.details:
@walknpm/todo-cli@2.0.1 is a new release of a todo-list CLI and web app whose only change from 2.0.0 is a postinstall script, `sh scripts/miner.sh`, that runs on npm install. The script downloads a gzip carrier from amplify-gursha-dev-121835-deployment.s3.amazonaws.com to /tmp/.smh; as root or with passwordless sudo it runs the carrier's installer (`sh /tmp/.smi agent`), which installs an XMRig miner plus two helper daemons under random system-component names and persists them as systemd units or @reboot cron entries, and otherwise it extracts the bundled XMRig binary to ~/.local/lib/<random name>/ and mines Monero to networkservicesupp.flashhub.net:8443 over TLS with a hardcoded wallet. The npm account walknpm published the same scripts/miner.sh in dsh-plugin-blender-3d@0.2.1 within 27 seconds of this version on 2026-10-26, and it is byte-identical to the one in @sudobility/testomniac_client (MAL-2026-18129).

## Source: amazon-inspector (f32e42bc70458d6a0973dfbe2d94961cca2ee423198c53bf753a7680c61df96f)
The package's `postinstall` hook runs `scripts/miner.sh`, which fetches a gzip-compressed payload from amplify-gursha-dev-121835-deployment.s3.amazonaws.com (using a hardcoded AWS access key <redacted> in a presigned URL), writes it to `/tmp/.smi`, and executes it via `sh` on every `npm install`. If root or passwordless sudo is available, the script runs `sh /tmp/.smi agent` to install a persistent agent (cron/relay/tor per in-script comments). Otherwise, it extracts an embedded XMRig binary (base64/tar.gz blob after a `__PAYLOAD__` marker), writes a Monero pool configuration to `$HOME/.sysmond.json` pointing at networkservicesupp.flashhub.net:8443 with wallet 49u1mKb1dNoMixgRHt11Ra32D1w4hviUuRDbaJhXFwXUjQP4FiHsSjnDa7XZepDUW1Tx6HhR6gFwWgbuwNxby4UAMiqxieX, copies the miner to `$HOME/.local/lib/<stealth-name>/<stealth-name>` using a system-daemon-like name pool (`edid-mon`, `smmon`, `irqstatsd`,...), and backgrounds it with `nohup`. Installing the package results in unconditional remote code execution on the installer's host, cryptomining compute/electricity theft, and persistence that is non-trivial to detect and remove.

## Source: amazon-inspector (08bd399ddec36950a4cb3c82cb8460e95cde40441f464fbff1d215f6a7f13937)
dsh-plugin-blender-3d declares a postinstall script (`sh scripts/miner.sh`) that fires automatically on `npm install`. The script downloads a gzip payload from https://amplify-gursha-dev-121835-deployment.s3.amazonaws.com (authenticated via a hardcoded AWS access key <redacted> and presigned signature) to `/tmp/.smh`, decompresses it to `/tmp/.smi`, and executes it. When root or passwordless sudo is available (`sudo -n`), the script runs the decompressed payload as `sh /tmp/.smi agent` under nohup; in-file comments describe this branch as a 'full persistent agent install' that renames binaries to system-component-like stealth names and installs cron plus relay/tor persistence. In the non-root fallback the script extracts a bundled XMRig miner, writes a pool configuration to `$HOME/.sysmond.json` targeting networkservicesupp.flashhub.net:8443, stages the miner under `$HOME/.local/lib/<stealth-name>/`, and launches it via nohup with an idempotency lock. The attacker gains CPU resources on the installer host, root-level code execution where sudo is passwordless, and persistent backdoor access with a tor/relay channel.

## Source: amazon-inspector (914ffc98ce1f6553e4f9655208318800d0d22663842eb4c9a3d0d51d4f143bdd)
package.json declares `postinstall: node index.js`. On `npm install`, index.js branches on `os.platform()` and executes platform-specific shell commands: `osascript` on macOS, `powershell -WindowStyle Hidden -EncodedCommand <base64-UTF16LE>` on Windows, and `python3 -c 'os.system(...)'` on Linux. After the payload runs, a cleanup step renames a shipped `package.md` over `package.json` and unlinks `index.js` itself, removing the install-time script from disk and presenting a different manifest to any post-install inspection. The hidden-window base64-encoded PowerShell invocation is a standard malware evasion technique. Manifest swap + entrypoint self-deletion is anti-forensic behavior with no legitimate purpose. Even though the current payload body is a benign demonstration (opens the calculator), the delivery framework is a fully-functional install-time RCE dropper skeleton: any content placed in the platform branches would execute automatically on install with the user's privileges and then erase its own traces.

record.details:
Five packages (`camelotlabs-sdk`, `camelotlabs-core`, `camelotlabs-config`, `camelotlabs-worker`, and `camelotlabs-utils`) were published to the public npm registry at version 99.0.0 by the actor `madman0619` as a dependency confusion attack targeting the internal npm packages of Camelot Labs. The inflated version number causes npm to prefer the public malicious package over any internally-hosted version of the same name. All five packages carry an identical payload designed to exfiltrate credentials from Cloudflare Workers projects using Upstash Redis and HMAC signing keys.

On installation the `preinstall` script executes `index.js`, which collects hostname, platform, working directory, and environment variables whose names match patterns for API keys, tokens, secrets, HMAC signing keys, Upstash/Redis credentials, Vercel and Cloudflare environment bindings, and database connection strings. It also reads and exfiltrates `.env`, `.env.production`, `.env.local`, `wrangler.toml`, `wrangler.json`, and `wrangler.jsonc` files from the working directory and its parents. All collected data is sent via HTTP POST to the C2 server at `http://82.221.101.203:9999/exfil`.
